_comment_profiles: Copy and rename these weave and output profiles to create your
own provider, prompt, routing, destination, and CRM mapping

_comment: A weave profile connects one configured provider to an
inline prompt or prompt file. This example uses
prompts/example.md.
This structured-extraction example asks the provider to
extract profile facts from a captured LinkedIn DOM.
Its output is placed beneath weave.linkedin.
The optional HighLevel plugin maps extracted LinkedIn facts
to a contact. Install transcript-weaver-highlevel before
using this profile.
Custom fields must already exist in the HighLevel location.
Every possible incoming field is mapped or ignored.
Different nonempty values stop for review by default.
This output profile routes Frank's transformed transcripts
to journals and an inbox. Copy and rename it for another
scheme.
This is the common root for every destination.
Every destination root, file, and directory is relative
to this vault.
Use relative_to only for relative vault paths.
Omit relative_to for absolute paths and paths beginning
with ~.
_comment_examples: CWD relative: path test-output, relative_to cwd.
Config relative: path test-output, relative_to config.

_comment: Dotted packet paths select the routing category and
the cleaned Markdown body inserted as the content
placeholder.
Reusable destination roots are relative to vault.
A destination selects one by name using its root field.
Files and directories are relative to their selected root.
Destinations without root are relative directly to vault.
Insert places a date heading and content in chronological
order. Duplicate dates get a separator and stderr warning.
Create writes one new file without overwriting another.
Formats support date, time, content, and dotted packet paths.
Filename placeholders are limited to date and time.
